Level: L5
Evidence family: gut_wall_efflux_intestinal_metabolism
Endpoint: oral_exposure_change_due_to_gut_wall
Result: AUC and Cmax increased significantly
Assay context: oral pharmacokinetic study in rats (single oral dose, plasma AUC and Cmax measured)
Conditions: "1,25(OH)2D3 (calcitriol) pretreatment"
Additional details: "The increased exposure is attributed to changes in intestinal membrane permeation rather than hepatic or renal first‐pass elimination."
Reported evidence: Oral administration of adefovir dipivoxil to rats pre‐treated with 1,25(OH)2D3 led to a significant increase in the AUC and Cmax of the active metabolite adefovir, indicating enhanced oral absorption of the prodrug and/or its metabolite.

Level: L5
Evidence family: gut_wall_efflux_intestinal_metabolism

Experimental details:
  - intestinal_site: enterocytes
  - substrate_status: substrate
  - transporter_or_enzyme: esterase

Additional details: "Conversion leads to systemic adefovir; statement based on study observations."
Reported evidence: Orally administered adefovir dipivoxil is rapidly converted into adefovir by esterase located in enterocytes, allowing the metabolite to reach systemic circulation.

Level: L5
Evidence family: gut_wall_efflux_intestinal_metabolism
Endpoint: efflux_or_secretory_transport
Result: substrate transporter substrate status
Assay context: in situ intestinal perfusion of rat ileum
Conditions: "presence of verapamil (P‐gp inhibitor)"
Experimental details:
  - intestinal_site: ileum
  - substrate_status: substrate
  - transporter_or_enzyme: P-gp/ABCB1

Additional details: "Transport enhancement observed qualitatively; no numeric value reported."
Reported evidence: In the in situ intestinal perfusion of rat ileum, inclusion of the P‐glycoprotein inhibitor verapamil resulted in transport enhancement of adefovir dipivoxil, indicating that P‐gp‐mediated efflux limits its intestinal absorption.

Level: L5
Evidence family: gut_wall_efflux_intestinal_metabolism
Endpoint: bidirectional_permeability
Result: ~10‐fold increase in transport of total adefovir
Assay context: in situ intestinal perfusion of rat ileum
Experimental details:
  - intestinal_site: ileum

Additional details: "Compared with transport of parent adefovir."
Reported evidence: In the in situ intestinal perfusion of rat ileum, adefovir dipivoxil produced an approximately 10‐fold increase in transport of total adefovir relative to the parent compound.

Level: L5
Evidence family: gut_wall_efflux_intestinal_metabolism
Endpoint: intestinal_metabolism
Result: 93.6 %
Assay context: Caco-2 cell monolayer metabolic assay
Experimental details:
  - intestinal_site: Caco-2 cell monolayer (model of intestinal epithelium)

Additional details: "10 µM [3H]adefovir dipivoxil was used; intracellular esterases are responsible for hydrolysis."
Reported evidence: The dipivoxil prodrug was hydrolyzed almost completely in Caco-2 cells, as indicated by the fact that 93.6% of the total radioactivity in the basolateral compartment was accounted for by [3H]adefovir.

Level: L5
Evidence family: gut_wall_efflux_intestinal_metabolism
Endpoint: other_intestinal_transport
Result: no significant difference in remaining fraction of adefovir dipivoxil between groups
Assay context: in situ closed loop study in rat duodenum, jejunum, and ileum
Conditions: "1,25(OH)2D3‐treated rats vs control rats"
Experimental details:
  - intestinal_site: duodenum, jejunum, ileum

Reported evidence: In the in situ closed loop study, there was no significant difference in the remaining fraction of adefovir dipivoxil in the duodenum, jejunum and ileum loops between control and 1,25(OH)2D3‐treated rats.

Level: L5
Evidence family: gut_wall_efflux_intestinal_metabolism
Endpoint: bidirectional_permeability
Result: 6.3 % recovery after apical dosing; 65 % after basolateral dosing
Assay context: Caco‐2 monolayer permeability (recovery after apical vs basolateral dosing)
Experimental details:
  - intestinal_site: apical and basolateral membranes

Additional details: "Asymmetric recovery suggests predominant apical efflux and limited net absorption."
Reported evidence: Recoveries of adefovir dipivoxil, mono‐(POM)‐PMEA and adefovir after apical administration were 6.3 %, 68 % and 13 % of the dose, respectively, whereas basolateral administration yielded recoveries of 65 %, 20 % and 1.1 % of the dose, highlighting marked asymmetry in intestinal permeability.
